page: Microsoft Azure D192lds_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine from the Dldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs via hyper-threading. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 480 MB L3 cache. This server is configured with 384.0 GB of system memory, which yields a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It also includes a substantial 11339 GB of bundled local storage and is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores placing in the top 10% of tested systems. The system also demonstrates top-tier memory bandwidth for both cached small-block reads and uncached large-block read/write operations. Single-core performance is more moderate, with stress-ng single-core results falling in the middle 50%. Cryptographic and compression workloads perform exceptionally well, as evidenced by top-tier results in PassMark encryption and single-threaded gzip compression.

The D192lds_v7 is highly suitable for compute-heavy workloads, multi-threaded decompression, static web serving, and database operations, supported by top-tier Redis SET throughput and strong database benchmark scores. However, the low memory allocation of 2.0 GB per core represents a clear tradeoff, making it less suitable for memory-intensive applications. While prompt processing for large language models is highly efficient, text generation speeds vary, with small model text generation falling into the bottom 25%. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high compute density and massive local storage capacity, making it a viable option for high-throughput parallel processing where memory footprint is not the primary constraint.
